question.text: In a Forward Rate Agreement (FRA), if at maturity the reference rate is higher than the FRA rate, who pays the difference?

answer.text: The buyer of the FRA pays the bank
The bank (seller) pays the excess to the company (buyer)
Both parties share the difference equally
The difference is settled through the clearing corporation

explanation.text: The Logic: If at the end of the FRA period the six-month reference rate (e.g., LIBOR) is greater than the FRA rate, the bank that sold the FRA pays the excess to the company; if the reference rate is lower, the company pays the difference to the bank. The Trap: The FRA mechanism locks in a rate for the future period. If the reference rate rises above the FRA rate, the seller compensates the buyer; if it falls below, the buyer compensates the seller. Note: The settlement described above is the rate-lock cash-flow mechanism stated in the Series III-A workbook for FRAs.
